knowledge_gaps: The proposed experiment changes the loss, negative count, exclusion policy and potentially sequence weighting simultaneously. Without specifying the baseline objective and reduction, an improvement cannot be attributed specifically to increased competition.

Uncorrected cross-entropy over sampled candidates defines a sampled classification objective; it is not automatically an unbiased approximation to full-catalog softmax. State the intended objective and justify whether sampling correction is needed under prefix-dependent sampling without replacement.

The choice of 64 negatives lacks direct GRU4Rec evidence. Relevant comparisons with GRU4Rec's TOP1-max, BPR-max and established sampling methods are missing. These alternatives deserve consideration before proposing a different backbone.

Reproducibility requires exact baseline hyperparameters, catalog construction, handling of histories truncated by the sampler, a gradient-enabled training scoring path, and a concrete generated-predictor parity check covering all four routes. These are local implementation questions that literature searches cannot resolve.

The report lacks measured runtime and peak-memory estimates for candidate scoring and unique sampling. Difficulty 3 may underestimate implementation cost within the shared GPU budget; originality 3 is reasonable, while future potential 7 remains speculative.

No baseline validation scores or predeclared checkpoint-selection schedule are supplied. Anonymous training prefixes cannot establish generalization, raw margin magnitudes depend on score scale, and repeated validation selection can overfit. Uniform negatives may leave popularity shortcuts intact and do not directly address the qualitative intent complaints.
